executionScenarios.name: extracts-and-appends
executionScenarios.description: A customer message is parsed into fields and appended to the sheet
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The webhook receives the message 'Hi, this is Jane Doe, my number is +1 555 0100 and I'm interested in the Pro subscription.' The OpenAI extraction returns name 'Jane Doe', phone '+1 555 0100', product interest 'Pro subscription'. The Google Sheets append returns a success response for the new row.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The workflow executes without errors and appends one row whose fields correspond to the extracted name, phone number and product interest.

conversation.text: Create a workflow that receives a customer message, uses OpenAI to extract the customer name, phone number and product interest, then saves that data into a Google Sheet.
How does the customer message arrive, and which sheet should the extracted rows go into?

[The message arrives as the body of an incoming webhook request. The extracted rows go into a Google Sheet the user will pick at setup — leave the sheet/document selection for setup and don't block on it.
Credentials will be added later. If anything else is unspecified, choose a sensible default and build.]

description: Sourced from LangTracer thread 12b40dc0 (built + executed, funnelStep 05). Free-text-to-structured extraction: an inbound customer message arrives over a webhook, an LLM pulls out name / phone / product interest, and the fields are appended as a row to Google Sheets. Tests that the agent uses an LLM to extract discrete fields (not just echo text) and maps them into the sheet columns. Harness note: the Google Sheets append uses a resource-locator that stays blank for setup, so the execution can red at the Sheets node even on a correct build — carry correctness in the outcome expectations.
outcomeExpectations: The workflow is triggered by an incoming Webhook carrying the customer message.
An LLM step (OpenAI) extracts the customer name, phone number and product interest from the free-text message, rather than storing the raw message verbatim.
A Google Sheets append/create-row step writes the extracted name, phone number and product interest into separate columns.
